title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Garden Auditorium on 1966-07-30
lineage: SBD > MR > ?? > CDR > EAC (secure) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: A rough but listenable sound‑board capture of a raw 1966 Vancouver show, highlighted by a fiery “Hey Little One” and early jam energy.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard source that suffers from minor speed quirks, wow‑and‑flutter on the opening “Dancing in the Street,” and several missing cuts, but it remains clear enough to enjoy. Musically the set showcases an enthusiastic Jerry Garcia (notably on “Hey Little One”), strong early jams and a standout rendition of “See That My Grave Is Kept Clean.” Overall fans are split – some love the historic vibe while others are disappointed by the incompleteness.

ai_rating.rationale: Ratings range from 2½‑5 stars; most reviewers praise the performance despite noting missing songs and minor audio flaws, leading to an overall moderate‑high score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear sound but with wow‑and‑flutter on “Dancing in the Street,” slight pitch/speed inconsistencies, and several songs omitted from the tape.

standout_songs: See That My Grave Is Kept Clean
poor_songs: Dancing in the Street (wow/flutter, weak warm‑up)
show_quality.setlist_flow: One‑set show that starts a bit flat, warms up on “Cold Rain & Snow,” then builds into energetic early ’66 jams before fading out with the missing cuts.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Powerful early wail; crooning on “Hey Little One”; complains about lack of warm‑up time.
band_member_comments.Phil: Declines to sing “Bite The Diamond Light” and later joins in “New Minglewood Blues"; no specific performance comment.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocal on "I'm a King Bee" described as making ethnic musicologists quiver.
